result.title: EDA: Observe, Verify, and Assess for Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Depression Analysis
result.summary: Existing multimodal depression assessment methods often summarize long recordings into global behavioral descriptions. This leaves the source and decision relevance of individual observations difficult to inspect. We propose EDA, an evidence-grounded framework organized around Observe, Verify, and Assess. In Observe, literature-informed acoustic and visual cues are localized into source-linked Evidence Records with temporal intervals and behavioral measurements. In Verify, frozen multimodal agents examine whether the cited media support each observation. The simplified Support admission policy retains positively verified records and their review grounds. In Assess, statistical descriptors and temporal events support reference-based behavioral comparison, while PHQ-9-guided text analysis provides complementary symptom evidence. Cross-modal disagreement triggers review of the original text before final selection. Experiments on D-Vlog and LMVD evaluate human-referenced cue agreement and downstream assessment utility separately. AI cue annotations achieve 91.02% accuracy against human consensus labels on shared source segments. With a frozen 7B backbone, EDA Support improves F1 over direct prediction by 7.61 and 9.88 percentage points on D-Vlog Leave-Query-Out and LMVD, respectively. These findings support explicit, source-linked behavioral evidence for inspectable multimodal depression assessment.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 EDA 框架，把抑郁评估拆为 Observe（将声学与视觉线索定位为带时间区间和测量的、可溯源 Evidence Record）、Verify（冻结多模态代理核查媒体是否支持该观察，仅保留通过验证的记录）、Assess（统计描述与时间事件做参照比较，并结合 PHQ-9 文本分析）三步，在 D-Vlog 与 LMVD 上评估线索一致性与下游效用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「证据需可溯源并被视觉核查后才准入」的门控设计，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与 latent 内容贡献分配提供可供核查的参考；但该工作属特定任务应用，未涉及 latent 推理状态生成。
